gapAnalysis.title: Anemic domain model — FileEntity/ItemModel has zero behavior
gapAnalysis.detail: ItemModel is a 90+ property data bag with public setters and no methods. All business rules that should live on the aggregate (checkout guard, delete guard, rename uniqueness, folder-type guard) are implemented as static methods in FileWriter.cs and FileCheckpoint.cs. State mutations such as setting checkout status or soft-deleting are performed directly on the DTO by the writer layer with no invariant protection.

gapAnalysis.title: Business logic in application layer — ActivationWriter enforces domain invariants
gapAnalysis.detail: ActivationWriter.ActivateContents contains multi-line domain rules: it checks item.VersionActivationStage == ContentVersionStatus.Published to throw ActivateActivatedVersionException, verifies variant uniqueness via LINQ GroupBy, and enforces the primary-version-must-exist rule. These are domain invariants that must be enforced inside ContentVersionEntity aggregate methods.

gapAnalysis.title: Static writer/reader classes bypass DI — untestable and uninjectable
gapAnalysis.detail: FileWriter, ActivationWriter, RenameItemCommon, FolderWriter and 15+ other writer classes are static. Controllers call them directly (FileWriter.AddFile(), FileWriter.DeleteFile()). Context and orchestrators are created via OrchestratorFactory and new ScopedExpressContext() inside the static methods. This makes business logic untestable in isolation and impossible to mock, and means DI-registered services cannot be substituted.

gapAnalysis.title: Domain repositories contain raw SQL — infrastructure leaks into domain layer
gapAnalysis.detail: FileRepository, ItemRepository, FolderRepository, and 27 other repositories extend SQLDataRepository and embed raw T-SQL strings with SqlParameter arrays. The repositories are located in the domain project (LibraryService.Domain) but are tightly coupled to SQL Server. There is no query abstraction; changing persistence requires touching domain-layer files.

gapAnalysis.title: Checkpoint classes externally enforce invariants that belong on aggregates
gapAnalysis.detail: 30+ *Checkpoint.cs classes in Express.Orchestrator/Checkpoint/ validate preconditions and throw exceptions before reaching any domain object. E.g. FileCheckpoint throws FileNotFoundException, FolderCheckpoint throws NoPermissionException. These are domain invariants; they should be enforced by aggregate methods, not by separate static validation classes upstream.

gapAnalysis.title: ContentEventConsumer uses fire-and-forget Task.Factory.StartNew with no await
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEventConsumer.ConsumeEvent spawns a LongRunning Task via Task.Factory.StartNew with _ = discarding the task handle. Exceptions inside RunConsumeAsync are caught only at the inner retry loop; an uncaught exception silently kills the consumer. Additionally Kafka offset is committed unconditionally (subscriber.Value.Commit called outside the tenant-match branch), meaning events for other tenants are silently dropped but their offsets advance.

gapAnalysis.title: Invariants enforced outside aggregates
gapAnalysis.detail: All domain invariant checks (file writable, file locked, file belongs to team site, version expirable) live in SystemStateExecutor and FileWriter rather than inside aggregate methods on FileEntity or FileVersionEntity. This means the rules can be bypassed by calling the repository directly.

gapAnalysis.title: Business logic in Express Writer layer
gapAnalysis.detail: FileWriter, PublishWriter, and ActivationWriter contain branching business logic (publishability checks, checkout ownership, custom property validation) that belongs in domain aggregate methods. These classes act as a de-facto domain layer without the encapsulation guarantees.

gapAnalysis.title: State transitions set externally on entities
gapAnalysis.detail: Workflow status (SUBMITTED, REJECTED, PROMOTED) and system state flags are set directly on model properties from application-layer code (e.g. item.WorkflowStatus = STATUS_SUBMITTED) rather than through protected aggregate command methods that enforce valid transitions.

gapAnalysis.title: Service Locator anti-pattern
gapAnalysis.detail: ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService<T> and GetScopedService<T> are used throughout FileWriter and OrchestratorFactory to resolve dependencies at runtime, creating hidden coupling and making unit testing impossible without the full DI container.

gapAnalysis.title: OrchestratorFactory hides 30+ implementations
gapAnalysis.detail: OrchestratorFactory creates orchestrators for 30+ operation types behind a single factory method. Actual dependencies (repositories, providers, Kafka clients) are invisible at the composition root, making static analysis and testing extremely difficult.

gapAnalysis.title: Service locator used throughout instead of constructor injection
gapAnalysis.detail: ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService<T>() is called 1,482 times across the codebase (SearchProducer.cs, ContentEventConsumer.cs, and hundreds of Reader/Writer classes). This is a well-known anti-pattern that defeats IoC, makes unit testing impossible, and hides dependencies. Every class resolves its own dependencies at runtime rather than declaring them via constructor parameters.

gapAnalysis.title: Static Reader/Writer classes replace application services and domain objects
gapAnalysis.detail: 70+ Reader and Writer classes (FileWriter, FolderWriter, PublishWriter, ActivationWriter, PermissionWriter, ExtensiveFileWriter, SBPProfileWriter, etc.) are used as static-style facades called directly from controllers (e.g. FileController.cs calls FileWriter.AddFile(), FileReader.ReadUnifiedContents()). These classes contain thousands of lines of mixed business logic, validation, persistence calls, and Kafka publishing. There is no application service layer or domain model layer — all behavior lives in these Reader/Writer monoliths.

gapAnalysis.title: Domain entity status mutated directly outside aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: Content item status is mutated directly on model objects in Writer classes rather than through aggregate command methods. Examples: ExternalSyncWriter.cs line 204 (itemVersion.Status = STATUS_UPLOAD_VIDEO_FOUNDATION_PROCESS_STREAM), line 211 (itemVersion.Status = isOfficeDocOrMedia ? ... : STATUS_READY), FileVersionWriter.cs line 1570 (newArticleVersion.Status = ItemStatus.STATUS_READY), SBPProfileWriter.cs lines 1423-1537 (repeated status checks and mutations). No invariant protection around state transitions.

gapAnalysis.title: Validation scattered across 40+ Checkpoint classes instead of aggregate invariants
gapAnalysis.detail: Business validation rules are encoded in 40+ procedural Checkpoint classes in the Orchestrator project (FileCheckpoint, FilePublishableCheckpoint, FileDeletableCheckpoint, ActivateCheckpoint, PromoteCheckpoint, FolderDeletableCheckpoint, ItemNameTooLongCheckpoint, etc.). These checkpoints execute guard logic that belongs inside aggregate command methods. The result is that business rules can be bypassed by calling Writer methods without running the associated checkpoints.

gapAnalysis.title: Two incompatible exception hierarchies with no typed DomainExceptionType
gapAnalysis.detail: The codebase has two distinct exception bases: ContentManagerException in ControlCenter.Core.Exceptions.Common (with ContentManagerExceptionCategory enum: Unknown/NotFound/InvalidParamter/NoPermission/ServiceUnavaliable/WorkflowDisabled) and ContentManagerException in LibraryService.Abstractions.Exceptions. Neither maps cleanly to HTTP status codes through a single DomainExceptionType enum. 150+ specific exception classes exist but are thrown from all layers including domain, infrastructure, and even controllers.

gapAnalysis.title: Controllers bypass application service layer and call Reader/Writer directly
gapAnalysis.detail: Controllers across all API versions (V1.0, V1.1, V2.0, Unified, Orbit, APIM, Dark) resolve business operations by directly instantiating or calling static-style Reader/Writer classes. Example: FileController (V1.0) calls FileVersionReader.ReadLatestVersion() and FileWriter.AddFile() with no intervening application service. FileController (Unified) calls FileReader.ReadUnifiedContents() and ExtensiveFileWriter.AddContent(). This means controllers contain implicit orchestration logic.

gapAnalysis.title: Domain project contains infrastructure concerns
gapAnalysis.detail: The Domain project houses infrastructure classes: NodeRepository (SQL queries), GoogleDriveRepository, ExternalSyncRepository, UserSettingRepository, SearchProducer (Kafka publisher), CacheRemoverClient (HTTP calls), ExternalSyncService (orchestration), MicroAppRepository. None of these belong in a domain project — they are infrastructure adapters. The real domain has no home.

gapAnalysis.title: Static Writer/Reader classes replace injectable Application Services
gapAnalysis.detail: Business logic lives in ~45 static classes (FileWriter, PublishWriter, FolderWriter, ContentViewReader, etc.) inside Seismic.ContentManager.Express. These classes create their own context via `new ScopedExpressContext()` inline and resolve dependencies via ServiceCollectionHelper service locator. They cannot be unit tested, mocked, or decorated. Every 'application service' method is a static entry point rather than a proper injectable IFileAppService/IPublishAppService.

gapAnalysis.title: Service Locator anti-pattern via ServiceCollectionHelper
gapAnalysis.detail: ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService<T>() and GetScopedService<T>() are called in ContentViewReader (~15 calls), ContentEventConsumer, FileWriter, and other static Express classes. This hides dependencies, makes constructor injection impossible, and breaks testability. The ILogger, ISeismicCacheProvider, IToggle, IFMSClientManager, and IMapperService are all resolved at call time rather than at construction time.

gapAnalysis.title: Anemic domain model — no aggregate roots with invariant methods
gapAnalysis.detail: FileManager, ItemManager are single-method thin delegators to repositories. FileVersionManager has no version state-transition methods. No entity class enforces business rules. All invariants (file cannot be published if checked out, version minorVersion != 0 blocks publish, name uniqueness) live in Checkpoint classes or Writer static methods rather than on aggregate root methods. ContentObjectStatus is a string-constants class rather than a typed enum or value object with valid-transition enforcement.

gapAnalysis.title: Business invariants enforced in Orchestrator Checkpoint layer instead of domain
gapAnalysis.detail: Seismic.ContentManager.Express.Orchestrator contains 40+ Checkpoint classes (FilePublishableCheckpoint, FolderOperableCheckpoint, PromoteCheckpoint, RenameCheckpoint, etc.) that enforce domain invariants — existence checks, permission gates, state pre-conditions — by throwing typed exceptions. These rules belong as guard methods on aggregate roots (e.g. FileEntity.Publish(), FolderEntity.Rename()). Moving them into the domain makes invariants co-located with state and testable without the full orchestrator stack.

gapAnalysis.title: Anemic FileEntity — state transitions live outside the aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: FileManager.cs delegates entirely to FileRepository with no invariant-enforcing methods. Checkout/undo-checkout transitions (IsCheckedOut, CheckedOutBy), soft-delete guards, and permission enforcement are all mutated directly from FileWriter and the Orchestrator RequestEditFileCheckpoint lambda. entity.Checkout() and entity.UndoCheckout() methods do not exist; any caller that bypasses the orchestrator silently bypasses all invariants.

gapAnalysis.title: All domain invariants encoded as Orchestrator Func factories, not aggregate preconditions
gapAnalysis.detail: IContentOrchestrator.RequestEditFileCheckpoint() returns a Func<> that performs permission checks, quota validation, parent-folder existence, and content-state guards. This means the complete domain rule set is encoded as application-layer factory lambdas. Any Writer or background service that creates its own ScopedExpressContext can call the underlying repository directly without going through any invariant gate.

gapAnalysis.title: PublishExecutor contains domain logic for publish-state transitions
gapAnalysis.detail: PublishExecutor.PublishFile() updates Profile state, validates publishability, and writes audit records across multiple direct repository calls with no transactional aggregate boundary. These are domain operations that should be expressed as PublishMappingEntity.Publish(actorId, profileId, folderLocations). The entity does not exist; the concept is fully procedural.

gapAnalysis.title: ExpirationJobExecutor owns the file-version expiration lifecycle
gapAnalysis.detail: ExpirationJobExecutor.Run() directly queries expired versions, marks them expired, removes publish mappings, and logs activity — all imperative steps that belong inside FileVersionEntity.Expire(). The domain invariant that a version must be removed from all publish profiles before being marked expired is encoded only in the executor's execution order, invisible to anyone loading a FileVersionEntity.

gapAnalysis.title: Controller couples directly to Writer classes without interface injection
gapAnalysis.detail: FileController calls FileWriter.ReadLatestVersion() and FileWriter.AddFile() with no IFileWriter interface injected. The controller has a direct compile-time or runtime coupling to the concrete Writer class, making it impossible to unit-test the controller in isolation and violating the dependency-inversion principle throughout the Controller → Writer layer.

gapAnalysis.title: Static Writer classes with no DI
gapAnalysis.detail: FileWriter, PublishWriter, FolderWriter, ItemBatchWriter, ActivationWriter, ExternalSyncWriter and 30+ other Writer classes are fully static. They instantiate ScopedExpressContext inline (new ScopedExpressContext()) and call OrchestratorFactory static methods. This makes them impossible to inject, mock, or test in isolation — and means the ambient request context is resolved at call time via a hidden global rather than being injected.

gapAnalysis.title: ServiceCollectionHelper static service locator
gapAnalysis.detail: ObjectLevelPermissionChecker, GlobalVariableCheckpoint and ContentEventConsumer call ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService<T>() to resolve ILogger, IServiceDiscoveryService, IHttpClientFactory, IClientCredentialsAuthentication, IToggle, and SeismicSettings. This is a service-locator anti-pattern: dependencies are hidden, lifetime mismatches go undetected at startup, and unit tests cannot substitute fakes.

gapAnalysis.title: Anemic domain models — all business logic in Writers
gapAnalysis.detail: ItemDemainModel, FolderModel, ContentVersionModel, FileDomainModel are pure data bags with only auto-properties and no methods. Business rules such as checkout guards ('if file.IsCheckedOut && file.CheckedOutUserId != userId throw'), non-publishable-type guards, version state transitions, and expiration date validation are spread across static Writer classes and Executor classes instead of being enforced by aggregate methods.

gapAnalysis.title: Business rules inline in PublishWriter — not on aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: PublishWriter.DeleteSchedulePublish contains: (1) checked-out-by-another-user guard, (2) teamSiteId ownership check, (3) non-publishable type check — all as raw if-throw blocks. These invariants belong on ContentObjectEntity.Publish() and ContentVersionEntity.Publish() aggregate methods so they cannot be bypassed by calling the repository directly.

gapAnalysis.title: Static god-object Express layer replaces all domain logic
gapAnalysis.detail: FileWriter, PublishWriter, ExpirationWriter, FolderWriter, AnnotationWriter and 25+ other static classes in Seismic.ContentManager.Express contain all business logic as static methods. Controllers call these directly (e.g. FileController calls FileWriter.AddFile). There are no injected domain services — the entire Express layer is an untestable, non-injectable transaction script.

gapAnalysis.title: Service locator anti-pattern used 1508 times
gapAnalysis.detail: ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService<T>() and GetScopedService<T>() are called 1508 times across the codebase. This hides all dependencies, makes unit testing impossible without a full DI container, enables circular dependencies, and bypasses the DI lifecycle guarantees. Used in static fields (ContentEventConsumer._logger), Lazy initializers (SearchProducer), and inline in domain/infrastructure methods.

gapAnalysis.title: No aggregate roots enforce business invariants
gapAnalysis.detail: FileManager.cs is 25 lines delegating to FileRepository with zero business logic. Batch-size limits (LIMIT_BATCHSIZE_CHECKOUT, LIMIT_BATCHSIZE_EXPIRENOW), state transition guards (cannot delete in workflow, cannot publish tiled without conversion), and uniqueness checks are all implemented as raw if-throw in static Writer methods, not as aggregate command methods.

gapAnalysis.title: Business logic embedded in infrastructure repository
gapAnalysis.detail: CustomPropertyRepository.cs contains a routing decision: if (Cms3Util.IsCMSCustomPropertyAPIEnabled(...)) it calls the CMS3 API path; otherwise falls back to the legacy SQL path. This is a domain policy (which system owns custom properties for this tenant) living in an infrastructure class, making it invisible to the domain layer and untestable without a real DB/HTTP context.

gapAnalysis.title: RefreshCacheService is a static service-locator-based utility
gapAnalysis.detail: RefreshCacheService.RefreshCache() is a public static method that resolves ISeismicCacheProvider via ServiceCollectionHelper inside a switch statement. It is impossible to inject, mock, or test. Cache invalidation is a domain concern (what to invalidate when an aggregate changes state) but is implemented as a static infrastructure utility called ad-hoc from Writer classes.

gapAnalysis.title: Controllers coupled directly to static Express methods — no application service boundary
gapAnalysis.detail: All 85 controllers inject only IServiceProvider and route calls directly to static FileWriter.AddFile(), PublishReader.ReadFileReferencedProfiles(), etc. There is no application service layer. This means the presentation layer is tightly coupled to implementation details, controller tests must exercise the full Express stack, and no use-case isolation is possible.

gapAnalysis.title: Static Writer/Reader classes use service locator pattern
gapAnalysis.detail: FileWriter, PublishWriter, ReviewWriter, FolderWriter and all other Express Writer/Reader classes create ScopedExpressContext via 'new ScopedExpressContext()' and resolve services via ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService<T>() / GetScopedService<T>() — completely bypassing the ASP.NET Core DI container. These classes cannot be unit-tested, cannot have dependencies replaced, and create ambient state via a hidden context object rather than explicit parameters.

gapAnalysis.title: OrchestratorFactory bypasses DI with direct construction
gapAnalysis.detail: OrchestratorFactory.CreateFolderOrchestrator(), CreateContentOrchestrator(), etc. construct concrete implementations directly (e.g. 'new SQLFolderOrchestrator(context)') instead of resolving from the DI container. This tightly couples all Writer classes to SQL implementations, prevents interface substitution for testing, and makes it impossible to register cross-cutting concerns via DI middleware.

gapAnalysis.title: ItemModel is an anemic domain model
gapAnalysis.detail: ItemModel contains 40+ public get/set properties including Status (string), VersionStatus (string), PublishStatus (string), ApprovalStatus (string), IsCheckedOut (bool), and IsExpired (bool) — all mutable from outside the class with no invariant enforcement. The only behavioral method is IsShortcut(), a read-only helper. State transitions are performed by Writer classes directly mutating these properties.

gapAnalysis.title: Business rules enforced in Writer layer instead of aggregates
gapAnalysis.detail: PublishWriter.DeleteSchedulePublish() contains file existence checks, cross-team-site ownership validation, checkout ownership checks, and content type publishability checks. ReviewWriter.AddContentReviews() contains user existence validation and review message composition. These are domain invariants that belong inside aggregate methods.

gapAnalysis.title: Anemic Domain Model: ContentObjectBase Is a Data Bag
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentObjectBase (545 lines) and ItemModel are pure data transfer objects. All business rules live in FileWriter.cs (~1500 lines) in the Express layer. The invariant 'a file may only be checked out by one user at a time' is enforced by a raw SQL UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK pattern inside FileWriter — not by the aggregate. Before: public bool IsCheckedOut { get; set; } public string CheckedOutById { get; set; } // no guard. After: public void Checkout(UserId userId) { if (_isCheckedOut) throw new FileLockedException(CheckedOutById); _isCheckedOut = true; _checkedOutById = userId; RaiseEvent(new FileCheckedOutEvent(Id, userId)); }

gapAnalysis.title: Static Service Locator Registered by All Controllers
gapAnalysis.detail: JsonApiControllerBase calls ServiceCollectionHelper.RegisterScopedServiceProvider(serviceProvider) — a static global setter — in every controller constructor. Express Reader and Writer classes resolve all dependencies from this static reference rather than through constructor injection. This makes the request scope ambiguous under concurrency, prevents unit testing without a full DI container, and creates a hidden singleton lifecycle for scoped services. Before: protected JsonApiControllerBase(IServiceProvider sp) { ServiceCollectionHelper.RegisterScopedServiceProvider(sp); } // then FileWriter.GetFile(). After: inject IFileQueryService and IFileCommandService via constructor; remove static service locator.

gapAnalysis.title: Raw SQL Executed Inside the Domain Layer
gapAnalysis.detail: FileRepository.cs, FolderRepository.cs, and ContentPermissionRepository.cs live in Seismic.ContentManagerService.LibraryService.Domain yet execute raw Dapper SQL strings including multi-hundred-line CTE queries. The 'domain' project concretely depends on SQL Server and Dapper. There is no repository interface abstraction at the domain boundary — the domain IS the infrastructure. Before: public async Task<ItemModel> GetFile(int id) { return await _db.QueryFirstOrDefaultAsync<ItemModel>("SELECT ... FROM ContentObject ..."); }. After: domain project defines IFileRepository; infrastructure project (Seismic.ContentManagerService.Infrastructure) implements it with Dapper, injected via DI.

gapAnalysis.title: Anemic File aggregate — version and rendition rules enforced in managers, not in domain
gapAnalysis.detail: FileRepository is a thin SQL wrapper. Business rules such as 'only one version is latest at a time', 'version numbers must be monotonically increasing', and 'renditions can only be generated for Active files' are implemented inside IFileVersionManager and IRenditionManager. Any caller that bypasses these managers (e.g. background services writing directly via IFileRepository) can violate these invariants silently. A rich ContentObject aggregate should enforce all version and rendition state transitions.

gapAnalysis.title: Expiration processing has no domain model — executor mutates content state directly
gapAnalysis.detail: ExpirationBackgroundService and ExpirationJobExecutor directly update content state in the database without routing through the File & Versioning aggregate. This means expiration transitions bypass ContentObject invariants: for example, re-activating an expired file could leave its version state inconsistent. No domain events (ContentExpired) are raised, so downstream domains cannot react cleanly.

gapAnalysis.title: No domain events raised for any state changes across the service
gapAnalysis.detail: None of the aggregates identified raise domain events (FileVersionCreated, ContentActivated, TeamSiteMemberAdded, etc.). State changes are persisted directly via repositories or manager classes. This prevents downstream domains from reacting to state changes through a clean event contract and forces tight coupling via HTTP or direct method calls. The absence of events also makes audit logging and eventual consistency patterns impossible without significant infrastructure work.

gapAnalysis.title: Permission evaluation logic in ContentPermissionRepository — 6-table JOIN in domain layer
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentPermissionRepository.GetPermissions() executes a 6-table JOIN (TeamSiteMember, TeamSiteMemberGroup, UserGroupMembers, PermissionDefinition, PermissionLevelPermissions, PermissionLevelMember) directly in the domain layer, coupling the domain to SQL schema details. Permission inheritance evaluation and effective access resolution belong in a domain service, not a repository. Additionally, PermissionController contains orchestration logic (check inheritance → break → re-grant) that belongs in an application service.

gapAnalysis.title: Anemic ItemModel — 89-property data bag with no business methods
gapAnalysis.detail: ItemModel and ItemVersionModel are pure data transfer objects with getters/setters and no business methods. All domain logic (move validation, copy rules, version activation guards) lives in Express Reader/Writer classes (FileReader, FileVersionReader, ActivationWriter, PromoteWriter). Business rules cannot be unit-tested without the full Express stack. Before: PromoteWriter directly sets version.PublishStatus = Published after reading current state imperatively. After: version.Promote() enforces invariants (workflow check, not-expired check) and internally queues a VersionPromotedEvent.

gapAnalysis.title: Layer violation — controllers directly invoke Express Readers/Writers containing SQL orchestration
gapAnalysis.detail: Controllers (FileController, VersionController, PublishController) inject and directly call Express Reader/Writer classes that mix application-level orchestration with raw SQL warehouse calls (Express.Warehouse/SQL/*.cs). There is no clean application service boundary between HTTP concerns and domain concerns. Before: FileController → injects FileVersionReader → calls ITransactionQueue.EnqueueStatement with raw SQL. After: FileController → calls IAddFileUseCase (application service) → calls FileAggregate.Add() → repository.Save(). The SQL lives in the repository only.

gapAnalysis.title: Infra coupling — 53 raw SQL files in Express.Warehouse bypass domain layer
gapAnalysis.detail: Express.Warehouse/SQL/ contains 53 files (File.cs, FileVersion.cs, Folder.cs, CustomProperty.cs, etc.) embedding raw Dapper SQL strings directly accessible from the application orchestration layer. Critical business state transitions (version publish, folder move) execute as bare UPDATE statements without passing through the domain aggregate, meaning invariants are never checked and domain events must be published separately by each caller. Before: ActivationWriter calls ITransactionQueue.EnqueueStatement(SQL.FileVersion.SetActiveVersion, params) directly. After: fileVersionRepository.Save(version) — the repository owns the SQL.

gapAnalysis.title: Controllers bypass domain model via Express layer
gapAnalysis.detail: FileController, FolderController, ItemController, PermissionController, PublishController, and MicroAppController call static Express Reader/Writer classes (FileWriter.AddFile, FolderWriter.AddFolder, PublishReader.ReadFileReferencedProfiles, etc.) directly — completely bypassing the domain service and manager layer. This means business invariants defined in FileManager or ContentPermissionManager are never enforced on the primary code paths. Two parallel data-access implementations exist for the same aggregate.

gapAnalysis.title: MicroAppManager registered but never used by MicroAppController
gapAnalysis.detail: MicroAppController injects nothing from the domain layer (no IMicroAppManager injection despite it being registered in DI) and routes all operations through ExtensiveFileReader/ExtensiveFileWriter. The domain manager is effectively dead code for this domain's primary API entry points. Business rules around Tiled workspace lifecycle are unprotected.

gapAnalysis.title: FileManager is an anemic pass-through with no invariant enforcement
gapAnalysis.detail: FileManager.GetFile is a single-line pass-through to FileRepository.GetFile. All file lifecycle rules (checkout, expiration, version ordering, sync config validation) live in Express writers or SQL stored procedures rather than on the aggregate. The ItemModel is a property bag with no domain methods.

gapAnalysis.title: Checkout invariant lives in application layer
ContentView business rules in application writer
Direct Dapper SQL in application-layer Readers and Writers
Anemic domain layer — business logic in static Express Writers
gapAnalysis.detail: FileManager has only GetFile(). FileVersionManager has only GetFileVersion() and GetLatestFileVersion(). ItemManager has only GetItemTeamSites(). All real business logic (add, copy, move, delete, checkout, activate, publish) lives in static application-layer Writer classes (AddFileCommon, CopyFileCommon, DeleteFileCommon, ActivationWriter, etc.). Domain aggregates enforce no invariants and emit no domain events.

gapAnalysis.title: No DomainException base class — 280+ raw exception types with no unified HTTP mapping
gapAnalysis.detail: All domain exceptions (FileNotFoundException, NoPermissionException, ActivateActivatedVersionException, etc.) extend System.Exception or application-specific bases with no shared DomainException<DomainExceptionType> contract. HTTP status code mapping is scattered across exception handlers. Adding a new exception requires updating multiple middleware layers. There is no DomainExceptionType enum to centralise code-to-HTTP mapping.

gapAnalysis.title: OrchestratorFactory static factory bypasses DI — 40+ orchestrators uninjectable
gapAnalysis.detail: OrchestratorFactory.Create*Orchestrator() methods construct orchestrators by resolving services via ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService() (a service locator). This means orchestrators depend on ambient static state, cannot be substituted in tests, and their dependency graph is invisible to the DI container. 40+ orchestrator interfaces are registered in DI but never actually injected — they are retrieved via the factory.

gapAnalysis.title: No value objects — status, tenant identity, and compound keys represented as raw primitives
gapAnalysis.detail: Content status is a raw string (item.Status = "published"), tenant identity is a raw string (teamSiteId), and compound version identity (contentId + versionId + variantId) is passed as separate string parameters everywhere. There are no immutable value objects with validation rules or equality semantics. This allows invalid states (e.g. empty status string, mismatched tenant) to propagate silently through the domain.

gapAnalysis.title: ScopedExpressContext created with 'new' inside writers — ambient tenant context not injected
gapAnalysis.detail: Every static writer method creates context via new ScopedExpressContext() or new WorkerExpressContext(tenantInfo, userId). This pulls current tenant/user from ambient thread state rather than from a well-defined IExpressContext injected through the request pipeline. Multi-tenancy correctness depends on thread-local state being set correctly upstream, which is fragile and invisible in tests.

gapAnalysis.title: Domain events not raised by aggregates — side effects triggered imperatively in writers
gapAnalysis.detail: After state changes (file deleted, content activated, content expired) the writers imperatively call observer/producer classes (LibraryContentReferencesObserver.Notify(), SearchProducer.Publish(), DataCollectionObserver.Notify()). There is no domain event raised from an aggregate method that the application service then dispatches. Side effect ordering and completeness depend on each writer remembering to call the right observers.

gapAnalysis.title: ExpirationJobExecutor and processor classes contain domain expiry rules
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentExpireProcessor and ContentExpireNotifyProcessor determine expiry thresholds and notification timing using SQL queries and inline logic rather than through a domain object method. The rule 'notify N days before expiration' is a domain invariant that should live on ContentExpirationEntity, not in a background job executor.

gapAnalysis.title: ScopedExpressContext couples domain to HTTP
gapAnalysis.detail: ScopedExpressContext holds a reference to the HTTP HttpContext as well as user identity, tenant info, permissions, and feature toggle state. Domain operations that accept this context are tightly coupled to ASP.NET Core middleware, preventing reuse in background services and tests.

gapAnalysis.title: ExpirationJobExecutor accesses warehouse SQL directly
gapAnalysis.detail: ExpirationJobExecutor calls into the Warehouse SQL layer directly with raw Dapper queries to find and expire versions, bypassing the domain aggregate and repository interfaces defined in the abstraction layer.

gapAnalysis.title: No aggregate root boundary on content graph
gapAnalysis.detail: File, FileVersion, FileVariant, FileAnnotation, and CustomPropertyValues are accessed independently through separate repositories. There is no aggregate root that controls the transactional boundary, allowing partial updates that can leave the content graph in inconsistent state.

gapAnalysis.title: Custom property validation in wrong layer
gapAnalysis.detail: CustomPropertyInvalidCheck and PropertyValueCalculatorUtils.BatchCalculatePropertyValues() are invoked from FileWriter (application layer) rather than from within the CustomPropertyEntity or a CustomPropertyDomainService, leaking domain validation into the orchestration layer.

gapAnalysis.title: Raw exceptions not mapped through DomainExceptionType
gapAnalysis.detail: Several classes throw raw framework exceptions (InvalidOperationException, ArgumentException, generic Exception) instead of typed ContentManagerException subclasses, causing HTTP status code decisions to be made inconsistently at the controller and middleware level.

gapAnalysis.title: Multiple API version controllers duplicating logic
gapAnalysis.detail: V1.0, V1.1, V2.0, V3.0 plus Dark/Orbit/APIM variants create 80+ controller classes with overlapping endpoint implementations. Cross-version logic differences are managed with if-branches and conditional DI rather than versioned application services.

gapAnalysis.title: Kafka event listeners contain domain logic instead of delegating to domain services
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEventConsumer, CustomPropertyEventListener, VFSEventListener, CrackingPipelineMetaEventListener, and AugmentationEventListener handle Kafka events using ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService<T>() and contain inline domain logic. They do not delegate to domain services or command handlers. VFSEventListener directly transitions file version status on video-processed events.

gapAnalysis.title: Missing value objects — status, type, and identity fields are raw primitives
gapAnalysis.detail: Content status values are compared as raw string literals and integer constants (e.g. 'if (item.Status == ContentObjectStatus.STATUS_GOOGLEDRIVE_PLACE_HOLDER)' scattered across 10+ Writer files). ContentType, Language, TenantId, TeamSiteId, and ContentId are all raw strings or GUIDs with no encapsulating value object enforcing validity. ContentObjectStatus is used as an enum but its transitions are not protected by a state machine.

gapAnalysis.title: Common.Model project is a 500+ file shared DTO dumping ground
gapAnalysis.detail: Common.Model contains 523+ files with all DTOs, request/response models, and shared constants mixed together with no domain separation. This creates implicit coupling across all bounded contexts — any model change risks breaking unrelated domains. There is no separation between domain model objects and API view models.

gapAnalysis.title: PropertyMessageController is a 432-line orchestration class in the controller layer
gapAnalysis.detail: PropertyMessageController performs complex nested-loop orchestration, maintains intermediate state, and executes multi-step batch custom property processing directly in controller action methods. This is orchestration that belongs in an application service or domain service.

gapAnalysis.title: No domain events raised on state transitions — search indexing is a direct call
gapAnalysis.detail: SearchProducer.ProduceAsync() is called directly from Writer classes without a domain event intermediary. When a file is published or activated, the Writer directly calls SearchProducer rather than raising a domain event (ContentPublished, ContentActivated) that a handler forwards to search. This couples business operations to infrastructure concerns and makes it impossible to add additional side effects without modifying Writer classes.
gapAnalysis.file: SearchProducer.cs (called directly from multiple Writer classes)

gapAnalysis.title: Seismic.ContentManager.Express.Orchestrator is a mixed-layer project
gapAnalysis.detail: The Orchestrator project mixes: Checkpoint validation classes (domain invariant logic), Orchestrator interfaces for HTTP clients (infrastructure), Cart and context-passing classes (application layer), and SQL orchestrators (infrastructure queries). It is a catch-all that prevents proper layer separation.

gapAnalysis.title: ExternalSyncService and ContentSyncManager coordinate sync without a domain abstraction
gapAnalysis.detail: ExternalSyncService.cs and ContentSyncManager.cs (in the Domain project) orchestrate multi-step external sync workflows procedurally. ContentSyncManager.cs line 282 catches ContentManagerException inline and branches business flow on exception type rather than on explicit domain state. This is infrastructure logic disguised as domain logic.

gapAnalysis.title: Domain project (LibraryService.Domain) contains HTTP client implementations
gapAnalysis.detail: RenditionHttpClient, PageStorageClient, DiscEventV2Client, GoogleDriveManager+AuthClient all live inside Seismic.ContentManagerService.LibraryService.Domain. A domain project must not contain HTTP clients or external-system coupling. These should live in an Infrastructure project with interfaces defined in the domain contracts.

gapAnalysis.title: ContentEventConsumer uses static fields and service locator instead of BackgroundService DI
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEventConsumer is a static class with static Lazy<> Kafka subscriber fields and static ILogger resolved via ServiceCollectionHelper. It lacks BackgroundService lifecycle management. Other listeners (CustomPropertyEventListener, VFSEventListener) follow a slightly better pattern but still use static subscriber dictionaries. All Kafka consumers should implement BackgroundService with constructor-injected IAvroClientFactory, IServiceScopeFactory, and ILogger.

gapAnalysis.title: Kafka publish embedded in Observer pattern inside Express — not domain events
gapAnalysis.detail: EventBusObserver, SearchMeshObserver, WebhookEventObserver, LibraryContentReferencesObserver, DataCollectionObserver all live in Seismic.ContentManager.Express/Notification. They are called from within Writers via a notification chain. The domain events they represent (ContentPublished, ContentDeleted, ContentUpdated) are not first-class domain event objects — they are constructed inline with raw data mapping inside the observer, making it impossible to test domain event semantics independently.

gapAnalysis.title: OrchestratorFactory uses static factory methods creating deep object graphs
gapAnalysis.detail: OrchestratorFactory.CreateTeamSiteOrchestrator(context), CreatePublishOrchestrator(context), etc. are static factory methods used inside every Writer. These factories create new orchestrator instances per call, bypassing DI lifetime management and making it impossible to swap implementations for testing without modifying static code.

gapAnalysis.title: Cart pattern couples domain query path to mutable HTTP-request-scoped state
gapAnalysis.detail: Cart.Cart is a request-scoped cache created in every Writer and threaded through all Orchestrators. Domain repositories short-circuit to the Cart before hitting SQL. This couples the domain read path to a mutable object tied to a single HTTP request, making aggregate loading non-deterministic and Cart invalidation bugs silently serve stale state to callers in the same request.

gapAnalysis.title: ActivityRepository.LogActivity called imperatively across 12+ layers
gapAnalysis.detail: Audit logging is an afterthought side-effect performed by direct repository calls from Executors, Orchestrators, Writers, and background services. There is no DomainEvent mechanism; adding a new content operation requires remembering to call LogActivity in the correct place. Omitting it silently produces an incomplete audit trail with no compile-time guard.
gapAnalysis.file: ActivityRepository.cs — called from ExpirationJobExecutor, PublishExecutor, SQLContentOrchestrator, FileWriter, and 8+ other classes

gapAnalysis.title: No domain events raised from entities; Kafka publishing is ad-hoc imperative
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEvent is published to Kafka via direct calls to DiscEventV2Client from PublishExecutor and background services. No aggregate raises a domain event; there is no DomainEvent base class, no domain event dispatcher, and no EventSender abstraction in the domain layer. Downstream Kafka consumers have no formal contract tied to aggregate lifecycle state changes.

gapAnalysis.title: 45+ bespoke exception classes instead of a DomainExceptionType enum pattern
gapAnalysis.detail: The service has 45+ custom exception classes (FileNotFoundException, NoPermissionException, ContentDeleteException, CheckoutException, etc.) all extending ContentManagerException directly without a typed enum. ExceptionMiddleware maps class types to HTTP codes. Adding new exception semantics requires two changes (new class + new middleware mapping), and there is no single place to audit all domain error states.

gapAnalysis.title: SQLDataRepository base exposes raw SqlDataReader to all repositories
gapAnalysis.detail: SQLDataRepository.ExecuteSqlReader() returns a raw SqlDataReader iterated manually in every repository. This binds all domain repositories to SQL Server connection semantics, makes repositories impossible to test without a live database, and leaks infrastructure-specific exception types (SqlException) into domain call stacks.
gapAnalysis.file: SQLDataRepository.cs — base class for FileRepository, FolderRepository, ProfileRepository, CustomPropertyRepository, and 10+ others

gapAnalysis.title: DomainActionProvider polymorphism for content types lives in the Express layer
gapAnalysis.detail: IDomainActionProvider / StandardDomainActionProvider / JourneyActionProvider / LessonActionProvider implement different behaviors per ObjectTypeId in an Express-layer DomainActionDispatcher. This content-type polymorphism belongs in the domain as a strategy on the ContentEntity aggregate, not as infrastructure-layer if/switch dispatch in the application orchestration module.

gapAnalysis.title: ItemStatus and ItemWorkflowStatus as raw string constants
gapAnalysis.detail: ItemStatus defines processing states as public const string fields (e.g. STATUS_READY = 'READY'). ItemWorkflowStatus does the same for workflow states (NONE, SUBMITTED, REJECTED, PENDINGPROMOTE, PROMOTED) and includes display-mapping logic that belongs on a value object. String equality comparisons scattered throughout the codebase mean typos are silent and exhaustive-switch analysis is impossible.

gapAnalysis.title: Raw inline SQL in all Repository classes
gapAnalysis.detail: FileRepository, FolderRepository, ItemRepository, and 10+ other repositories construct raw SQL strings inline with SqlParameter arrays and execute them via ExecuteSqlReader. Column names, table names, and query logic are hard-coded strings with no abstraction. A column rename requires grep-across-the-codebase; missing a usage causes a silent runtime failure.

gapAnalysis.title: Checkpoint layer mixes domain rules with infrastructure resolution
gapAnalysis.detail: The Checkpoint classes (ItemCheckpoint, FolderCheckpoint, FileCheckpoint, PromoteCheckpoint, RenameCheckpoint, ObjectLevelPermissionChecker) contain business invariant enforcement AND use ServiceCollectionHelper to resolve infrastructure. This mixed responsibility means the same class cannot be unit-tested for its domain rules without also mocking HTTP clients and logger singletons.

gapAnalysis.title: ExpirationBackgroundService drives domain state transitions
gapAnalysis.detail: ExpirationBackgroundService and ExpirationJobExecutor compare dates, decide whether to expire content, and call SQL updates directly. The expiration lifecycle (scheduled → notified → expired) has no representation on the ExpirationRuleEntity aggregate. The 'when to expire' logic cannot be tested without running the BackgroundService.

gapAnalysis.title: FileExtensionService orchestrates cross-domain logic from Domain project
gapAnalysis.detail: FileExtensionService lives in Seismic.ContentManagerService.LibraryService.Domain but coordinates ISystemIdentityManager, ITeamSiteMemberManager, and IContentPermissionManager — a pure application-layer orchestration concern. The 2000-member team site limit is enforced here, not in TeamSiteEntity. The service is named for a domain concept but performs use-case orchestration.

gapAnalysis.title: No domain events — Kafka publishes hardcoded inside Writer static methods
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEventSender and SearchProducer are called inline within FileWriter, PublishWriter, and ExpirationWriter after persistence calls. Domain events are not raised by aggregates and consumed by infrastructure handlers — instead, the publishing side-effect is procedurally hardcoded with no clear boundary between what the domain decided and what infrastructure did with that decision.
gapAnalysis.file: FileWriter.cs, PublishWriter.cs, ExpirationWriter.cs (Kafka publish call sites)

gapAnalysis.title: No value objects — all domain identifiers and statuses are raw strings
gapAnalysis.detail: teamSiteId, fileId, fileVersionId, profileId are all string parameters threaded through hundreds of method signatures. Version status is a raw string ('published', 'draft') compared inline. No VersionStatus enum with transition guards. No TenantId, TeamSiteId, or FileId value objects enforce format or prevent parameter transposition bugs.

gapAnalysis.title: TeamSite membership limit enforced outside the aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: The business rule 'a team site cannot have more than 2000 members' is enforced in FileExtensionService (application orchestration), not inside a TeamSiteEntity.AddMember() command method. Moving this invariant is a pre-condition for any refactor of the team site domain.

gapAnalysis.title: Tabeeb annotation subdomain embedded but structurally separate
gapAnalysis.detail: Tabeeb.Business.Domain and Tabeeb.Business.Common are self-contained bounded contexts with their own Entity, visitor pattern, and payload resolvers. They share no aggregate roots with the content domain. They could be extracted as a separate service or at minimum a clearly isolated bounded context within this service.

gapAnalysis.title: Status fields modeled as raw strings instead of typed value objects
gapAnalysis.detail: ItemModel.Status, ItemModel.VersionStatus, ItemModel.PublishStatus, and ItemModel.ApprovalStatus are all plain string properties. Invalid status values can be assigned silently with no compile-time safety, transition rules cannot be encoded in the type, and all callers must rely on magic strings for comparisons.

gapAnalysis.title: Multiple versioned controllers duplicate domain logic
gapAnalysis.detail: FileController exists in V1.0, V1.1, V2.0, and V3.0 namespaces; FileVersionController exists in V1.0, V1.1, V2.0, V3.0; TeamSiteController in V1.0, V1.1, V2.0, V3.0. Each version contains slightly different delegations to the same Writer classes, creating multiple entry points with duplicated cross-cutting logic and making it unclear which controller owns the domain.

gapAnalysis.title: Raw exception classes thrown without DomainExceptionType mapping
gapAnalysis.detail: The codebase throws FileNotFoundException, NoPermissionException, InvalidParameterException, CheckoutException, ActivateActivatedVersionException and 20+ other ad-hoc exception classes directly. There is no unified DomainExceptionType enum — the exception-to-HTTP mapping is scattered across catch blocks in controllers and middleware, making consistent error responses fragile.

gapAnalysis.title: Express.Tools contains domain logic that belongs in domain layer
gapAnalysis.detail: SearchMessageClient in Express.Tools checks a LaunchDarkly feature toggle to decide whether to route to Kafka or Azure Search, and constructs Kafka payloads inline. This routing decision is domain logic (which search index receives this content?) and should live in a domain service, not a shared tools library.

gapAnalysis.title: ContentObjectABTableRouter exposes DB table routing at domain model level
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentObjectABTableRouter is referenced in both Domain.Abstraction and LibraryService.Abstractions, exposing the A/B database table routing strategy as a first-class domain model. Domain entities should not know which database table stores them — this couples the domain model to a specific SQL schema optimization.

gapAnalysis.title: VersionNumber Not Modelled as a Value Object
gapAnalysis.detail: Version identity is two naked int properties (MajorVersionNumber, MinorVersionNumber) on ItemVersionModel. Increment, comparison, display, and equality logic is duplicated across callers. Before: public int MajorVersionNumber { get; set; } public int MinorVersionNumber { get; set; }. After: public sealed record VersionNumber(int Major, int Minor) { public VersionNumber IncrementMajor() => new(Major + 1, 0); public VersionNumber IncrementMinor() => new(Major, Minor + 1); public override string ToString() => $"{Major}.{Minor}"; }

gapAnalysis.title: MaterializedPath Not Modelled as a Value Object
gapAnalysis.detail: LibraryMaterializedPath is a raw string on FolderModel and ContentObjectBase. Path construction, ancestor extraction, and descendant LIKE queries (WHERE path LIKE '/x/y/%') are repeated in raw SQL inside FolderRepository. Before: public string LibraryMaterializedPath { get; set; }. After: public sealed class MaterializedPath { private readonly string _value; public MaterializedPath Append(Guid childId) => new($"{_value}{childId}/"); public bool IsAncestorOf(MaterializedPath other) => other._value.StartsWith(_value); public string ToLikePattern() => $"{_value}%"; }

gapAnalysis.title: Domain Events Not Raised by Aggregates
gapAnalysis.detail: State transitions (file published, version created, content deleted, permission changed, file checked out) do not raise domain events from within aggregates. Kafka messages are published directly from FileWriter, PublishWriter, and BulkupdateWriter in the Express layer via Notification.Notification.AsyncBroadcast(). This means a domain state change can occur without the Kafka event being emitted if the Writer call is bypassed, and there is no single source of truth for what events a given state transition produces.

gapAnalysis.title: Custom Property Values Stored as XML Blob
gapAnalysis.detail: CustomPropertyXml on ContentObjectBase is a raw XML string parsed on-demand via GetOrParseCustomPropertyXDoc() with three separate lazy-loaded dict caches (_customPropertyNameDict, _customPropertyIdDict, _customPropertyIdNameValueDict). Azure Search indexing must parse this XML to extract field values. There is no typed CustomProperty value object. Before: public string CustomPropertyXml { get; set; } + XDocument.Parse(). After: public IReadOnlyList<CustomProperty> CustomProperties { get; } where CustomProperty is a value object with typed PropertyId, Name, and Value, serialized at the persistence boundary only.

gapAnalysis.title: God Aggregate: One ContentObject Backs All Content Types
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentObjectBase backs files, folders, shortcuts, MicroApps, Articles, Learning Journeys, LiveDocs, and Email Templates — differentiated only by integer constants in ContentObjectType.cs (e.g., CONTENT_TYPE_MICROAPP = 19, CONTENT_TYPE_LIBRARY_FOLDER = 98). These concepts have distinct lifecycles and invariants. Conditional branches (if (contentType == 12) ...) appear throughout the codebase instead of polymorphic dispatch. A Folder aggregate should not share a class with a MicroApp.

gapAnalysis.title: Five publish controllers with overlapping responsibilities — no unified PublishTask aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: PublishController, SchedulePublishController, SimplifiedPublishController, ActivationController, and PromoteController each handle different facets of the publish lifecycle independently. There is no single ContentPublishTask aggregate enforcing 'a file must be in Draft before scheduling' across all entry points. Different callers may apply different eligibility checks, creating inconsistent publish behaviour per entry point.

gapAnalysis.title: CustomPropertyRepository makes inline HTTP call to Cms3Util — infra in domain layer
gapAnalysis.detail: CustomPropertyRepository calls an external Cms3Util API directly during a repository read to fetch API-enabled property definitions. This couples the domain layer to an HTTP dependency and violates infrastructure isolation. The Cms3Util adapter should be placed behind a domain interface (IApiPropertyProvider) resolved at the application service layer, keeping the repository a pure data-access object.

gapAnalysis.title: Custom property cache invalidation depends solely on external Kafka message
gapAnalysis.detail: When a custom property definition is updated locally, no domain event is raised. Cache coherence relies entirely on an external Kafka message arriving via CustomPropertyEventListener. If the message is delayed or lost, the cache serves stale property definitions. A domain event from the CustomPropertyDefinition aggregate should trigger cache invalidation synchronously or via a guaranteed local outbox.

gapAnalysis.title: OAuth tokens stored as plain strings — no OAuthToken value object
gapAnalysis.detail: GoogleDriveRepository persists OAuth tokens via IContentManagerContext without a value object enforcing token encryption at rest, expiry validation, or refresh semantics. Treating OAuth tokens as plain strings means token expiry is only discovered at call time (resulting in sync errors) rather than proactively surfaced by the value object's invariant check.

gapAnalysis.title: MicroApp lifecycle entirely delegated to external TiledClient — no local domain model
gapAnalysis.detail: MicroAppRepository delegates all MicroApp CRUD to an external TiledClient HTTP call. The content-manager-service cannot enforce MicroApp invariants (e.g. 'a MicroApp must have a valid tile configuration before publishing') without an HTTP round trip to an external service. This couples the domain model to external service availability and response shape.

gapAnalysis.title: Missing value objects — domain IDs and statuses modeled as primitives
gapAnalysis.detail: Throughout the codebase, domain identifiers (ContentId, VersionId, TeamSiteId, FolderId) are typed as string or Guid with no strong typing. Statuses (PublishStatus, WorkflowStatus) are bare enums without encapsulated validation behavior. This allows any string to be passed as any ID with no compile-time safety. Before: FileRepository.GetFile(string fileId) — a FolderId string can be passed silently. After: FileRepository.GetFile(FileId fileId) where FileId is a value object with a private constructor and validation.

gapAnalysis.title: Missing state machine — version lifecycle not enforced on aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEventTypeEnum defines event types covering the full version lifecycle (CreateFileVersion → PromoteContent → PublishContent → VersionExpired) but transitions are not enforced by a state machine on ItemVersionModel. PublishWriter and ActivationWriter independently set overlapping publish-related flags without shared guard logic, risking conflicting states (e.g., a version being both Expired and Published). Before: PublishWriter checks version.IsExpired then sets version.PublishStatus = Published. After: version.Publish() throws InvalidOperationException if lifecycle state is not Approved, using a sealed state machine.

gapAnalysis.title: Layer violation — FolderModel.CustomPropertyXml exposes XML serialization as domain field
gapAnalysis.detail: FolderModel.CustomPropertyXml is a raw XML string on the domain model, requiring callers to invoke CustomPropertyXmlResolver to read property values. XML is an infrastructure serialization concern leaking into the domain model. Before: folder.CustomPropertyXml parsed by CustomPropertyXmlResolver.Resolve(folder.CustomPropertyXml) at call sites. After: folder.CustomProperties returns a typed CustomPropertyCollection value object; XML serialization is the repository's concern.

gapAnalysis.title: Missing concept — domain events published imperatively by writers, not raised by aggregates
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEvent with its event types is published imperatively from Express Writer classes (PublishWriter.PublishFile calls eventBus.Publish(new ContentEvent(PublishContent))) rather than being raised by aggregates during state transitions. This requires every Writer to remember to publish the correct event; omitting the publish call silently breaks downstream consumers. Before: PublishWriter → updates DB → publishes ContentEvent(PublishContent). After: version.Publish() internally queues VersionPublishedEvent; domain event dispatcher publishes after transaction commits.

gapAnalysis.title: Anemic TeamSite — owner invariant unenforceable without aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: TeamSiteMember operations are direct repository calls without loading the owning TeamSite aggregate first. The invariant 'a team site must always have at least one owner' cannot be enforced because TeamSiteMemberRepository.RemoveMember(teamSiteId, userId) executes without loading full team state. Before: TeamSiteController → TeamSiteMemberRepository.RemoveMember() directly. After: teamSite = teamSiteRepository.Load(teamSiteId); teamSite.RemoveMember(userId); // throws if last owner teamSiteRepository.Save(teamSite).

gapAnalysis.title: NodeManager has no domain behaviour — pure data retrieval
gapAnalysis.detail: NodeManager.GetNodeAsync delegates directly to NodeRepository with no additional logic. NodeDomainModel is a plain DTO. The node graph's materialized path invariant (parent chain consistency on move) is not enforced at the domain layer.

gapAnalysis.title: ExternalSyncManager is a thin delegation layer without domain events
gapAnalysis.detail: ExternalSyncManager.UpdateConnectionStateAsync calls the repository directly with no domain event raised. The state change that enables/disables sync configs is a multi-step side-effect (ExternalSyncService orchestrates it) but produces no auditable domain event and no rollback path if ContentSyncManager.EnableSyncConfigAsync fails mid-way.

gapAnalysis.title: BSSService contains infrastructure concerns directly in the domain layer
gapAnalysis.detail: BSSService calls TenantBlobProvider, VideoThumbnailUtil, and DataStore.AddDeleteObject directly — these are infrastructure adapters that should be behind an interface. Blob byte manipulation, SAS URL construction, and video thumbnail extraction are in the domain service, making it untestable without a real blob store.

gapAnalysis.title: Cache invalidation is imperative and dispersed rather than event-driven
gapAnalysis.detail: PeerTalk cache invalidation is called from scattered call sites (Express writers, service methods) rather than being triggered by domain events. There is no guarantee that cache is invalidated every time state changes; the responsibility is manual and error-prone.

gapAnalysis.title: No domain events raised on content lifecycle state changes
gapAnalysis.detail: There are no explicit DomainEvent classes raised within aggregates on file creation, publish, expiration, or permission change. Downstream effects (search reindex, cache bust, notification) are triggered imperatively from service methods rather than by subscribing to domain events. This makes side-effect tracking invisible and coupling implicit.

gapAnalysis.title: FolderRepository executes raw ADO.NET SQL inline
IsNonPublishableType check duplicated across two writers
No domain events raised on publish or expiration
gapAnalysis.detail:
FilePublished and FileVersionExpired are significant state transitions that downstream services (search, analytics, profile caching) need to react to, yet they produce only a generic Kafka ContentEvent with a type flag rather than typed domain events. PublishWriter builds the event payload inline (strings, dictionaries) rather than using a named domain event class. This makes the contract implicit and fragile.

After: Introduce FilePublishedEvent, FileVersionExpiredEvent domain event types in Seismic.ContentManagerService.LibraryService.Abstractions.Events.Model, raised by the domain aggregate and dispatched by the application layer.

gapAnalysis.title: Cross-aggregate repository access in FileVersionManager
gapAnalysis.detail: FileVersionManager depends on IFileRepository (not IFileVersionRepository) to retrieve versions. FileVersions should be accessed through the File aggregate root or a dedicated FileVersionRepository, not by bypassing aggregate boundaries with the parent's repository.

gapAnalysis.title: Custom property values stored as XML strings in aggregate root
gapAnalysis.detail: ItemModel.CustomPropertyXml is a raw XML string containing all property values. Parsing logic (GetCustomPropertyIdNameValueDict, CustomPropertyTextSearch, CustomPropertyAzureSearch) is embedded directly in the entity, creating a hidden value object that should be a proper typed class. This also makes property access O(n) parse operations.

gapAnalysis.title: FakeMode static flag leaks testing concern into domain classes
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentPermissionManager and TeamSiteMemberManager both expose `public static bool FakeMode` which, when set, redirects calls through ServiceCollectionHelper.GetScopedService (service locator anti-pattern). Infrastructure/testing concerns should not exist in domain classes.

gapAnalysis.title: Missing domain events — state transitions emit Kafka events directly from application layer
gapAnalysis.detail: No explicit domain event types model state transitions (ContentPublishedEvent, VersionActivatedEvent, ContentExpiredEvent). Kafka messages are produced directly in Express Writer static methods via SearchProducer without routing through domain aggregate events. This bypasses domain boundary enforcement.

gapAnalysis.title: Kafka consumer group ID uses non-production naming convention
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEventConsumer creates a consumer group with GroupId = cms-test-consumer-{topic}. The 'test' infix in a production consumer group ID risks conflicting with actual test consumers and makes observability tooling harder to distinguish environments.

gapAnalysis.title: RLPolling background service uses Thread.Sleep instead of async delay
gapAnalysis.detail: ExpirationBackgroundService calls Thread.Sleep(sleepMillis) inside an async ExecuteAsync method, blocking the thread pool thread for the sleep duration. Should use await Task.Delay() to release the thread during idle periods.

gapAnalysis.title: Orchestrator layer duplicates permission checking already done in controllers
gapAnalysis.detail: Multiple orchestrators re-validate permissions (tenant access, user role) that are already enforced by the [Authorize] attribute and policy middleware on the controller. This creates divergence risk: a permission change must be applied in two places.

gapAnalysis.title: WorkflowRequestProxy is a pure HTTP passthrough
gapAnalysis.detail: WorkflowRequestProxy contains zero domain logic — it is a typed HTTP client masquerading as a domain service. Local workflow status is not enforced: the service cannot protect against invalid status transitions when the external workflow service is unavailable.

gapAnalysis.title: No domain events raised internally
gapAnalysis.detail: The service publishes Kafka events after persistence but raises no in-process domain events. This means cross-domain reactions (e.g. expiration triggers permission cleanup) must be handled by the application layer, creating temporal coupling and making side-effect chains hard to trace.

gapAnalysis.title: Batch operations allow partial failure silently
gapAnalysis.detail: BatchUpdateFileCustomProperties catches per-item exceptions and continues, returning a mixed success/failure result without any rollback of prior successful items. There is no compensating transaction or saga to restore consistency on partial failure.

gapAnalysis.title: Tenant context passed as parameter, not encapsulated
gapAnalysis.detail: tenantId and teamSiteId are passed as explicit parameters through every method call stack rather than being encapsulated in a TenantContext value object resolved once at the request boundary. This causes widespread coupling to multi-tenancy infrastructure in domain methods.

gapAnalysis.title: RenditionReader sets Rendition status directly on view model during read
gapAnalysis.detail: RenditionReader.cs lines 178, 204, 212, 216 set skimmer.Status = RENDITION_STATUS.READY/PROCESSING/NOTEXIST directly inside a read operation while mapping data. Status derivation logic for rendition availability belongs in a RenditionEntity or domain service, not in a reader/mapping class.

gapAnalysis.title: Tabeeb.Business.Domain and Tabeeb.Business.Common are orphaned external domain fragments
gapAnalysis.detail: Two projects (Tabeeb.Business.Domain, Tabeeb.Business.Common) exist as source code within the service repo but represent a different product domain (Tabeeb). These should either be extracted to their own service or clearly identified as a separate bounded context rather than being embedded in content-manager-service.

gapAnalysis.title: ContentObjectStatus as untyped string constants with no state machine
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentObjectStatus is a class holding string constants (STATUS_READY, STATUS_FAILED, STATUS_UPLOAD_POST_UPLOAD_PROCESSING, etc.) with a raw string Status property. There is no enforcement of valid transitions, no exhaustive enum for compile-time safety, and status comparisons use raw string equality throughout the codebase. This should be a proper enum or sealed class with allowed-transition logic.

gapAnalysis.title: Exception types are ad-hoc custom classes not mapped through a DomainExceptionType enum
gapAnalysis.detail: The codebase has 20+ ad-hoc exception classes (FileNotFoundException, NoPermissionException, DuplicateNameException, SchedulePublishTaskNotFoundException, etc.) each inheriting from ContentManagerException or NuPitchRequestException. There is no central DomainExceptionType enum to map to HTTP status codes, making error-handling middleware complex and HTTP status decisions scattered. A unified exception pattern would allow a single ExceptionFilter to handle all domain exceptions.
gapAnalysis.file: ContentManagerException.cs, FileNotFoundException.cs, NoPermissionException.cs, DuplicateNameException.cs (and 15+ others in LibraryService.Abstractions/Exceptions/)

gapAnalysis.title: Cart pattern in Orchestrator accumulates context without explicit aggregate identity
gapAnalysis.detail: The Cart class (Seismic.ContentManager.Express.Orchestrator/Cart/Cart.cs) is passed through every Checkpoint chain and Writer to accumulate validated data (file, user, folder). This is a mutable bag-of-objects pattern that obscures which aggregates are loaded and what state has been validated. It conflates the loaded domain objects with the validation context, making it hard to reason about what has been verified at any point in the flow.

gapAnalysis.title: 30+ Orchestrator interfaces fragment domain logic across the application layer
gapAnalysis.detail: IContentOrchestrator, IFolderOrchestrator, IPermissionOrchestrator, IPublishOrchestrator, IUserOrchestrator, ITeamSiteOrchestrator, IProfileOrchestrator (30+ total) each hold fragments of domain logic. A single business operation such as AddFile requires creating and coordinating three Orchestrators — complexity that DDD resolves by having one aggregate enforce its own invariants with a single command method.

gapAnalysis.title: Warehouse layer duplicates repository abstractions already defined in LibraryService
gapAnalysis.detail: Express.Warehouse defines IFile, IFolder, IPermission, IProfile warehouse interfaces that duplicate IFileRepository, IFolderRepository, IContentPermissionRepository, IProfileRepository in LibraryService.Abstractions. Two parallel repository abstraction layers add indirection without adding isolation; changes to persistence contracts must be made in two places.

gapAnalysis.title: LaunchDarkly feature-toggle concerns wired directly into controllers via filter attributes
gapAnalysis.detail: Controllers use [DeprecatedByToggleFilter(FEATURE_STATEBASEDPUBLISHING)] attributes that invoke the LaunchDarkly SDK at the controller level. Feature flags are an infrastructure concern and should be resolved in an application service or middleware, not declared as routing attributes on controller actions.

gapAnalysis.title: ContentEventConsumer is non-functional dead code
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEventConsumer.ConsumeEvent has the actual consume call commented out (// result = ConsumeEventOnce(...)). The RunConsumeAsync path only logs the raw JSON and calls Commit without delegating to any domain handler. This consumer is registered but performs no domain action, suggesting an incomplete or abandoned feature.

gapAnalysis.title: Missing typed domain exception hierarchy
gapAnalysis.detail: The codebase uses a mix of custom exceptions (FileNotFoundException, FolderNotFoundException, NoPermissionException, InvalidParameterException, DuplicateNameException from ControlCenter.Core.Exceptions) but there is no single ContentManagerException base with a typed DomainExceptionType enum that maps to HTTP status codes. HTTP status mapping is done implicitly by exception type in middleware, meaning new exceptions require middleware changes.

gapAnalysis.title: Duplicate exception hierarchies with no DDD mapping
gapAnalysis.detail: Two parallel exception hierarchies exist: ContentManagerException (in LibraryService.Core.Exceptions, 100+ subclasses) and NuPitchWarningException / NuPitchFatalException (in Common.Model). Neither hierarchy is structured around domain concepts — they are named after technical error conditions. HTTP status mapping happens in a central exception filter, not via a DomainExceptionType enum that the domain layer owns.

gapAnalysis.title: Background services contain domain orchestration logic
gapAnalysis.detail: ExpirationBackgroundService, ScheduleActivateBackgroundService, and ScheduleAddToProfileBackgroundService do not delegate to domain services — they call Express Executor/Writer static methods directly, mixing scheduling infrastructure concerns with business process execution in one class.

gapAnalysis.title: Cart pattern is a mutable shared-state bag passed through all Express methods
gapAnalysis.detail: Cart.Cart is instantiated at the top of every Writer static method and threaded as a parameter through the entire call chain to accumulate lazy-loaded data. This is a home-grown unit-of-work/context bag that bypasses DI scoping, makes call flows impossible to follow, and couples all Express components to a shared mutable object rather than explicit dependencies.

gapAnalysis.title: Domain.Abstraction project mixes interfaces with concrete DTO/model classes
gapAnalysis.detail: Seismic.ContentManagerService.Domain.Abstraction contains both interface definitions (e.g. IFileService) and concrete model/DTO classes (e.g. FileModel, FileVersionModel). Consumers of the abstraction layer must take a dependency on concrete data structures, violating the purpose of an abstraction layer and making it harder to evolve the model independently of the interface contracts.

gapAnalysis.title: Content Type Discriminated by Magic Integer Constants
gapAnalysis.detail: Content types are integer constants scattered across ContentObjectType.cs and checked via raw integer comparisons throughout FileRepository, FolderRepository, and ItemController. Invalid type IDs can enter the domain without error. Before: public const int CONTENT_TYPE_ARTICLE = 12; if (obj.TypeId == 12). After: public enum ContentType { Presentation = 1, Article = 12, MicroApp = 19, LibraryFolder = 98 } with factory methods that prevent construction of invalid typed aggregates.

gapAnalysis.title: Cart/Checkpoint Pattern Obscures Aggregate Invariant Ownership
gapAnalysis.detail: The Express Orchestrator layer uses a Cart/Checkpoint pattern to coordinate multi-step operations (e.g., CheckoutFile goes through ContentOrchestrator.RequestEditFileCheckpoint(cart, CMOperationType.CheckoutFile)). While this provides authorization gating, no single aggregate class owns the file-checkout invariant. A reader of the domain model has no way to discover that 'only one user can check out a file at a time' — it is enforced in OrchestratorCheckpoints, invisible to the aggregate. This violates the DDD principle that aggregates are the consistency boundary.

gapAnalysis.title: Media processing retry and quarantine logic embedded in Kafka listener
gapAnalysis.detail: BlobVirusScanEventListener.RetryPostProcessVirusScanEvent implements exponential backoff retry with domain decision-making (quarantine vs. allow) inline in a background service. This mixes infrastructure concerns (Kafka consumption, retry scheduling) with domain logic (determining scan outcome consequences). The quarantine decision should be delegated to a domain service or policy object.

gapAnalysis.title: FileVersion and FileVariant accessible via independent repositories — aggregate boundary bypassed
gapAnalysis.detail: FileVersionController and FileVariantController each call repositories that can create and modify version/variant records independently of the parent ContentObject aggregate. A FileVersion should only be created or modified through its ContentObject aggregate to maintain lifecycle invariants like monotonic version numbering and single-active-version constraints.

gapAnalysis.title: Activity records have no immutability guarantee — no append-only domain model
gapAnalysis.detail: ActivityController exposes both write and read endpoints for activity records with no domain model enforcing immutability. Activity entries should be append-only (event-sourced or insert-only) to provide a reliable audit trail, but there is no aggregate invariant preventing modification or deletion of recorded activity events.

gapAnalysis.title: Missing concept — no explicit aggregate roots in domain project layer
gapAnalysis.detail: The Domain projects (Seismic.ContentManager.Domain, Seismic.ContentManagerService.LibraryService.Domain) contain only Service and Repository classes. The closest things to aggregates are model classes in the Abstractions projects, which are shared DTOs used across layers. There is no single authoritative place that owns and protects the invariants of any bounded context, making it impossible to enforce DDD consistency boundaries at the domain layer.

gapAnalysis.title: Improvement — single 61-type ContentEventTypeEnum conflates events from 8 domains
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEventTypeEnum contains event types spanning Content, File Versioning, Folder, Content Lifecycle, Permissions, Custom Properties, Content Views, and Variants in a single enum. This forces all Kafka consumers to subscribe to the monolithic content-event topic and filter by type rather than subscribing to a domain-scoped topic. Splitting into aggregate-scoped event enums (FileEvent, VersionEvent, FolderEvent, PermissionEvent) co-located with their aggregates would align topic partitioning with the bounded context model and reduce consumer coupling.

gapAnalysis.title: ItemModel / NodeDomainModel use primitive strings for typed fields
gapAnalysis.detail: Fields such as Status, VersionStatus, PublishStatus, Format, OriginType, and ObjectTypeId are raw strings or ints rather than value objects or enums. This allows invalid state to be stored and forces all consumers to do string comparison rather than type-safe dispatch.

gapAnalysis.title: ContentSyncManager dependency on both Google and OneDrive clients creates hidden coupling
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentSyncManager receives IContentSyncClient registrations for GoogleContentSyncClient and OneDriveContentSyncClient via TryAddEnumerable — the manager must enumerate and dispatch to the correct client. This is a strategy pattern without explicit strategy selection logic, leading to implicit coupling between sync source type and client implementation.

gapAnalysis.title: TiledClient has no domain interface
gapAnalysis.detail: TiledClient in Seismic.ContentManager.Domain/MicroApp/TiledClient.cs is a concrete HTTP client registered directly; MicroAppManager depends on it by concrete type. The domain project should depend on an ITiledClient interface so the Tiled integration can be stubbed in tests and swapped without touching domain logic.

gapAnalysis.title: CustomPropertyXmlResolver contains parsing + validation logic outside aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: CustomPropertyXmlResolver and CustomPropertyDefinitionResolver in the domain project parse XML property definitions and resolve values, but they are standalone helpers rather than methods on the CustomPropertyDefinitionModel aggregate root. Property schema validation should be an invariant of the aggregate, not a utility class called from the manager.

gapAnalysis.title: ProfileRepository is a plain SQL repository with no domain behaviour
gapAnalysis.detail: ProfileRepository contains only data-access methods; all profile-related business logic (version existence, SBP eligibility) is validated via Checkpoints in the orchestration layer (ProfileVersionExistanceCheckpoint, ProfileExistanceCheckpoint). These are domain invariants that belong on ProfileModel rather than on infrastructure checkpoints.

gapAnalysis.title: ItemModel represents both files and folders via IsFolder flag
gapAnalysis.detail: ItemModel has an IsFolder property that switches its meaning. Files and folders are distinct concepts with different lifecycles and invariants but share one entity class. This inflates the aggregate and makes type-specific invariant enforcement impossible without if/else branching.

gapAnalysis.title: WorkflowRequestProxy is a pure HTTP proxy with no domain logic
gapAnalysis.detail: WorkflowRequestProxy contains only HTTP forwarding with no domain invariants (e.g., preventing publish of pending-review versions should be enforced here). Workflow state impacts File & Versioning lifecycle but no guard exists at the domain boundary.

gapAnalysis.title: ExpirationPolicy is not a first-class aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: Expiration date is stored as a nullable field on ItemModel (ExpirationDate) rather than as a separate ExpirationPolicy aggregate. ExpirationBackgroundService iterates raw DB queries instead of loading domain aggregates. Expiration business rules (notification lead time, auto-unpublish) are scattered across ExpirationJobExecutor, ContentExpireProcessor, and ContentExpireNotifyProcessor.

gapAnalysis.title: Content Rendering has no domain representation — thin proxy only
gapAnalysis.detail: RenditionHttpClient, ContentViewReader, and ContentViewWriter are purely infrastructure/application-layer components with no domain aggregate for rendition state. Rendition lifecycle (Pending → Processing → Ready → Failed) is not modeled, making it impossible to enforce that a content item may not be published without a ready rendition.
